finding_reviews.rationale: Coverage is right (D06 is fund-level: 31/86 issuers at 2026-06-30) and the position-id count reproduces (83 of 150 own-book rows carry a 2026-03-31 position id). The conclusion does not hold. The investigator's own two quotes show the filer prints the identical name 'JFL-Atomic AcquisitionCo, Inc.' in both filings, so the proposal reason 'd06-issuer-spelling-differs-between-filings' is contradicted by the source. The discontinuity is the build's: published issuer names for 2024-09-30 to 2026-03-31 are humanised member names ('JFL Atomic Acquisition Co Inc', 'Lead Venture Inc', confirmed in holdings) that differ from the page, which the report itself records as a parked shared defect. D06 here surfaces a real published-data error, so false_alarm is the wrong conclusion. Needs confirmed_error (pointing at the parked issuer-name repair) or an owner decision to accept the known defect, with a reason that does not attribute it to the filer.

The decision existing_detector / D06 does not catch recurrence: the rationale itself says D06 'does not fire while the wrong form is stable', so a fund that always uses explicit members gets no finding. The suggested_check written (D06 below 50 pct with position-id continuity above 50 pct) is a new check, so this should be propose_detector, or a page-name comparison.

existing_detector cites 'observations.py show gics-label-depends-on-build-composition', which is an entry in the observations log (4 funds, open), not a rule or a disposition proposal. No ledger rule flags a GICS label changing between builds, so recurrence would not be detected. Should be propose_detector (the suggested_check is concrete) or not_feasible with a reason.
